---
title: "Creating Quarto Reports and Presentations"
---

Quarto documents combine text, code, and results in one file. Write the source in a file ending in `.qmd`, then render it to create an HTML file you can open in a web browser. Your data analysis should still be conducted in R script. Quarto should be used only to generate the final report or presentation, by pasting the relevant code and output into the `.qmd` file.


## Create a report

In RStudio, choose **File > New File > Quarto Document**. Select **HTML** (default) as the output format, give the document a title, and save it with a name such as `my_report.qmd`.

RStudio should give you a template file. Pay attention to how you start a new section/slides, and how you add code chunks.

As an example, view the [lecture 9 slides](../lectures/lecture_9/lecture_9_slide.html). The source Quarto file can be downloaded [here](../lectures/lecture_9/lecture_9_slide.qmd){download="lecture_9_slide.qmd"}.

Click **Render** in RStudio.  The rendered file is `my_report.html`. Open it in a browser to check the layout, text, code output, and figures before sharing it.

To import a data in a qmd file, you need to specify the correct file path.  For simplicity, I recommend placing the data file in the same directory as your `.qmd` file and use `read.csv("your_data_file.csv")` to import it.


## Create a presentation

In RStudio, choose **File > New File > Quarto Presentation**. Select **Revealjs** as the output format (default), give the presentation a title, and save it with a name such as `my_slides.qmd`.


## Submission

You should only submit the rendered HTML file, not the source `.qmd` file.
